messages:
Maya Nguyen: Hey folks — landing my first tiny change to api-proxy. Quick q: what commit message format and branch naming should I use for a small timeout tweak?

Samir: welcome onboard, Maya! Use Conventional Commits for the message. Branching: fix/<short-desc> for bugfixes or feat/<short-desc> for new stuff. Example commit message we like:
```
fix(proxy): lower default request timeout to 5s

Closes: #USER-1234
```
Keep the PR focused and add a short test plan.

Devon: Also run the preflight locally: `./scripts/preflight.sh`. It runs lint + a couple unit tests. And run `pre-commit install` once so hooks fire automatically.

olivia-k: For reviewers, pick one from CODEOWNERS and one domain reviewer if the change touches infra or infra-adjacent code. Labels we use: `needs-review`, `size/XS` (for tiny PRs), and `backlog` if you don't need quick turnaround.

Jake L: Small tip — keep commits atomic. If you accidentally include an unrelated tweak, split it out. For PRs under ~10 LOC we often squash on merge, but still keep the branch tidy.

ci-bot: [ci] build triggered — lint/tests running (#4372)

Maya Nguyen: thanks — where's CODEOWNERS located? I couldn't find it at the repo root.

Samir: it's under `.github/CODEOWNERS`. If a path isn't covered, default reviewers are `@platform-team`.

Devon: Pre-commit uses black + prettier + isort. If formatting fails, run `./tools/format` before pushing.

olivia-k: Minimal PR checklist to paste in your description:
1) short summary + why
2) related issue/links
3) test plan (how you verified)
4) tag reviewers / owners
5) run preflight & CI green
Add `size/XS` label if it's very small.

Jake L: If you DM me or drop a message here when it's up I can give a quick review. Usually a <15min turnaround for small stuff.

Maya Nguyen: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-proxy/pull/78 — small timeout change. Ran preflight locally, CI pending. tagging @Jake L and @olivia-k

ci-bot: [ci] build #4372 passed — all checks green :tada:

Samir: Merging now. Congrats on the first one and welcome again! :wave:

Maya Nguyen: Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast help!
